title: Failure to face the truth: why avoiding hard facts blocks strategy, teams and companies
summary: Jason Cohen argues that a primary blocker of progress is refusing to face the truth, in feedback, meetings and strategy. He draws the pattern across Radical Candor, Five Dysfunctions, Good Strategy Bad Strategy and Good to Great (Kroger vs. A&P), and shows how fluffy language hides it.

principles.text: Failure to face the truth is a primary, invisible blocker of progress, because denial and rationalization are our default mode.
principles.quote: A primary blocker of progress, from our personal lives to our corporate strategies, is a Failure to face the truth.

principles.text: Strategy must name the monster in the room: write down the scary challenge crisply, then build a plan that attacks it head-on.
principles.quote: In every strategy discussion, there's a monster in the room no one will name, even though the point of strategy is to identify and then construct a battle plan against the monsters.

principles.text: Use meetings to surface insights; in most meetings someone is thinking something and not saying it.
principles.quote: In almost every meeting, someone is thinking something and not saying it, even though one of the best uses of a meeting is to unveil and discuss insights.

principles.text: Telling someone the truth is a courtesy, and withholding it is impolite at best and ruinous at worst, but it needs a foundation of trust.
principles.quote: The truth is a courtesy; conversely, failure to face the truth is at least impolite, and at worst "ruinous" in Scott's terminology

principles.text: Great teams build trust first so that it is safe to have constructive conflict and discuss the real issues together.
principles.quote: We must have enough trust in each other to face the truth, together.

principles.text: Seeing the truth isn't enough. Companies that win act on it; A&P saw the superstore data and shut the test down, while Kroger pivoted.
principles.quote: A&P saw the truth, but failed to face the truth.
